title: Shadowgrid onboarding eval — runtime/kernel diffs (flash attn, paged KV, cont-batching)
content:
Summary:

This is the shadowgrid run log for onboarding `shadow-model-v1` (65B opt-quant) through the runtime variations we plan to ship: flash-attn enabled (fa-v2), paged KV cache on, and continuous-batching at low/med/high thresholds. Goal: identify behavioral and perf deltas introduced by kernel/runtime changes before rolling to canary.

Top-level findings (short):
- Performance: flash-attn (fa-v2) reduces p50 token latency by ~12–18% vs baseline attn on A100 80GB when sequence < 1024; win shrinks for long-context (> 2k) due to paging overhead.
- Paged KV: turning on paged-KV gives 22–45% token-cost reduction for multi-turn chat (prefix reuse) but increases p95 latency tail for some tail-heavy prompt distributions when page eviction thrashes.
- Continuous batching: lower thresholds (batch target 8 tokens) reduce p95 by ~10% at cost of throughput; aggressive batch sizes (target 64) max throughput but shows 1.8x spike in transient latency under request-bursty workloads.
- Behavioral/regression: small but measurable token-choice deltas on 7% of instruction-following prompts (mostly formatting / code-block punctuation). No catastrophic semantic regressions observed.

Experiment setup (shadowgrid mechanics):
- Shadowgrid: mirrored traffic split from hosted canary endpoint to a non-production runtime cluster. Each request clones into 3 variants and compares outputs asynchronously: baseline-runtime (stock kernels), fa-v2 + paged-kv + contbatch-low, fa-v2 + paged-kv + contbatch-high.
- Prompts: 125 prompt-set mix (see below). We log per-token latencies, end-to-end latency, logprobs for top tokens, final text, stop-token alignment, and model logits sample for a small subset.
- Hardware: A100-80GB (primary), a small Ampere 1xA10 cluster for stress tests.
- Duration: 72h continuous, ~210k shadowed requests collected.

Prompt set breakdown (representative):
- IF-Short (40 prompts): direct instruction following, single-turn, examples: 
  - "Convert the following list into a bulleted checklist: 1) Verify backup 2) Notify team 3) Close incident"
  - "Write a 2-line commit message summarizing: Fixed off-by-one in index calculation"
- IF-Long (30 prompts): long-context summarization (2–3k tokens context), examples: meeting transcript -> TL;DR
- Code (20 prompts): small function completion and formatting, examples: python function to parse ISO timestamps
- Multi-turn chat (20 prompts): 6–12 turn sessions reused KV cache
- Edge-formatting (15 prompts): tables, markdown code fences, numbered lists

Key metrics captured (per-variant):
- latency_p50_token, latency_p95_token, latency_p99_token, e2e_latency, throughput_tps, tokens_per_usd_estimate, stop_token_alignment_rate, format_correctness_rate, hallucination_rate (spot-eval), avg_logprob_top1_delta (vs baseline).

Quantitative diffs (high-level):
- fa-v2 + paged-kv + contbatch-low vs baseline:
  - latency_p50_token: -15% (win)
  - latency_p95_token: +6% (slight regression)
  - e2e_latency on multi-turn: -28%
  - tokens_per_usd: +33% (much cheaper)
  - stop_token_alignment_rate: -0.9% (small regression)
  - format_correctness_rate: -1.6% (observed mostly on edge-formatting prompts)

- fa-v2 + paged-kv + contbatch-high vs baseline:
  - latency_p50_token: -18%
  - latency_p95_token: +22% (noticeable tail regressions under burst)
  - throughput_tps: +1.9x
  - tokens_per_usd: +72%
  - avg_logprob_top1_delta: mean change 0.03 bits (small but measurable)

Behavioral deltas (examples):
- Formatting drift: in 11/125 prompts, the new runtime emitted an extra trailing space inside code fences or included an extra backtick on closing fence. Example:
  - Prompt: "Return a markdown snippet with a bash command in a fenced block"
  - Baseline: "```bash
echo "hello"
```"
  - Variant: "```bash
echo "hello" 
``` " (extra trailing space inside fence)
  - Impact: downstream parsers that match fences strictly flagged invalid block in 2 customers' integration tests.

- Tokenization/stop alignment: paged-KV + contbatch-low case had 2–3% higher incidence of premature stop-token emission in long-context summarization when the prompt contained unusual delimiter sequences (— em-dash + emoji).

- Semantic shifts: observed 3 prompts where a numerical answer changed (e.g., currency rounding). Root cause hypothesized as subtle logprob recalibration following flash-attn float path differences (quantization paths changed rounding behavior).

Diagnostics and root-cause hypotheses:
1) Flash-attn float path: fa-v2 uses a fused kernel that slightly reorders reductions and uses different fp16 accumulation vs baseline. This can change tiny probability mass for borderline tokens -> formatting/space punctuation deltas.
2) Paged-KV eviction policy: current eviction uses LRU-ish heuristics tuned for prefix-reuse; under bursty multi-user mixes we see page churn that increases tail latency and occasionally drops KV segments leading to premature generation stops.
3) Continuous-batching scheduling: large target batch sizes have head-of-line blocking during bursty arrival, causing p95 spikes. Conversely, very small targets reduce batching benefit and hurt cost efficiency.

Repro steps for a few high-priority failures (notes for eng):
- Reproduce trailing-space formatting issue: take the failing prompt from the sample set (ID 73), run single-shot with same seed on baseline vs fa-v2 (deterministic run with top_k=1 sampling) and log token-by-token topk and emitted whitespace tokens. See GH PR #3214 instrumentation.
- Reproduce premature stop: craft long summary with embedded em-dash + emoji, run with paged-KV enabled/disabled; compare KV page hit/miss timeline and whether model emitted STOP after page miss.

Suggested mitigations and experiments to run (next 7 days):
- Short-term (quick wins):
  - Add whitespace-sensitive token-monitoring to the regression gate; fail rollout if format_correctness_rate drops >2%. Owner: Priya (applied-ml).
  - Reduce contbatch-high default from 64->48 for hosted canary to reduce p95 tail. Owner: Diego (serving-runtime).

- Mid-term:
  - Adjust flash-attn fp16 accumulation to match baseline accumulation order (perf cost estimate: ~1.5% latency increase) and re-run behavioral sweep on the 125 prompt set. Owner: runtime-kernels team.
  - Implement paged-KV eviction adaptive backoff for mixed workloads; add per-tenant page-thrash metrics to Console. Owner: platform-engineering.

- Long-term:
  - Add model-level micro-evals that check strict formatting invariants (code fence sanity, markdown AST roundtrip) as part of onboarding. Owner: applied-ml.

Open questions / risks:
- Can we tolerate a small formatting delta if cost savings are >30%? Which customers would be impacted? Needs CS input from product/SEs.
- Is there an exploitable nondeterminism introduced by fused kernels that could affect safety evals? Need research audit.

Immediate action items (triage board):
- [ ] Create a short-circuit rule in rollout: if format_correctness_rate < baseline - 2% then stop canary (Evelyn)
- [ ] Re-run the critical 11 edge-formatting prompts with debug-level token logs (Priya)
- [ ] Open perf/regression PR: reduce contbatch default on canary clusters (Diego)
- [ ] Schedule follow-up sync with SRE/Platform to instrument paged-KV eviction counters (Liam)

Appendix: sampled failing prompts and outputs (IDs):
- ID 12 (code fence): prompt text + baseline + variant (see diagnostic steps).
- ID 73 (markdown + emoji): stop alignment failure.
- ID 101 (currency rounding): numerical shift example.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a working log — not exhaustive. If we decide to ship fa-v2 + paged-kv, I recommend a staged rollout: 1) limited tenant opt-in with observability hooks for format/stop regressions, 2) kerneled fix for accumulation ordering, 3) wider rollout after 2 weeks of stable signals.

Slack threads / PRs referenced:
- slack: #runtime-kernel-updates thread 2026-03-10 -> https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02XXXXXX
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3214 (flash-attn changes)
- JIRA: INF-4721 (paged-KV eviction investigation)

If you want, I can extract the 11 edge-formatting failing examples into a small gist for CS to run against customer integrations.

-- Evelyn
